name: tool-row-click-collapses
opens_with: (/voice to clear the boot notice; three bash rows come from the agent script)
notes:
2026-11-03, plan plan-2026-11-03-tool-row-click-expand-acceptance.md, Change 4, collapse half. The single most valuable assertion pair in this scenario is `expanded_tool_id == "null"`: a stale-state regression (the toggle sets the id but never clears it, or clears it only on a DIFFERENT row) expands correctly on the first click and then lies forever after. The expand scenario alone cannot catch that; it never issues a second click.

`== "null"` is the DSL's Null comparison, not an empty string: evaluate_assertions (cmd_tui_debug.rs:1395) maps serde_json::Value::Null to the string "null" for ==. An empty-string comparison here would silently never match.

Same row twice, by design. `toggle_tool_expansion_by_id` is the ONLY place that clears the id, so a second click on the SAME row is the one gesture that reaches the collapse branch. Clicking a different row instead would move the expansion and never collapse — that is a different contract, and it is pinned by clicking_a_tool_row_toggles_that_call_only in-process.

Both scenarios share agent_script tool-row-expansion.json so the two differ in exactly one dimension (the number of clicks) and nothing else. That is what makes the pair a guard rather than two independent greens.
